blocks.en: Experiments collects the 25 protocol sheets behind ReLEAF’s wet-lab work, organized across four experimental stages and paired with downloadable procedures and diagrams.
blocks.text: Experiments collects the 25 protocol sheets behind ReLEAF’s wet-lab work, organized across four experimental stages and paired with downloadable procedures and diagrams.

blocks.en: The sheets follow four stages: ten for cloning, eight for protein production, five plant assays and two for the bioreactor. All but one carry the full procedure as a downloadable PDF, down to the reagent volumes and the arm the readout is scored against. The newest is the His-tag detection ELISA, which reads His-tagged protein against a six-point standard curve. Activity is measured instead by the DNPH assay, scaled down twenty-fold onto a 96-well plate. Three sheets produced no result on this wiki: the Bradford assay, large scale extraction, and purification and dialysis.

blocks.en: Overview
blocks.text: Overview

blocks.en: ReLEAF makes plant protectants in Bacillus subtilis and tests them on Arabidopsis under salt and heat stress. The wet lab work runs in four stages, and each hands its product to the next: cloning builds the constructs, protein production gets the protectant out of the culture and measures its activity, the plant assays test it, and the bioreactor sheets calibrate the instruments that watch the culture grow.

Summary

Whole-project experiment map: cloning in E. coli, electroporation into B. subtilis, bioreactor culture, secreted protectants, plant model testing on agar, soil and hydroponics, and plant growth evaluation by chlorophyll, root length, leaf area and fresh weight.
Protocol groups
Procedure diagram for culture agar preparation: weigh LB agar into a flask with water and glycerol, stir, autoclave, cool in the cabinet, add antibiotic, pour plates.
Procedure diagram for PCR amplification: assemble the reaction on ice, then run the thermal cycle.
Procedure diagram for restriction enzyme digestion: calculate the DNA volume, assemble buffer, enzyme, DNA and water on ice, incubate.
Procedure diagram for DNA gel electrophoresis: cast the agarose gel with stain, load ladder and samples, run at 100 volts, image.
Procedure diagram for Golden Gate assembly: combine vector, inserts, T4 ligase, buffer and type IIS enzyme, then cycle digestion and ligation.
Procedure diagram for heat-shock transformation: thaw competent cells on ice, add plasmid, heat shock at 42 degrees, recover in SOC, plate.
Procedure diagram for electroporation: grow and wash electrocompetent Bacillus subtilis, mix with plasmid in a chilled cuvette, pulse, recover in SOC, plate on selective agar.
Procedure diagram for colony PCR: grid a backup plate, pick each colony with a tip, streak it on the grid, drop the tip in a PCR tube with master mix, run the cycle.
Procedure diagram for liquid culture: label tubes, add TB medium and antibiotic, pick a colony with a tip, drop it in, incubate at a slant.
Procedure diagram for plasmid miniprep: pellet the culture, resuspend, lyse, neutralize, bind to the column, wash, elute, measure on the BioDrop.
Procedure diagram for the Bradford assay: dilute a BSA standard series, add standards and samples to a 96-well plate with Bradford reagent, incubate, read at 595 nanometers, fit the standard curve.
Procedure strip for harvesting the secreted fraction: centrifuge the culture, keep the supernatant, add protease inhibitor, clarify with a second spin.
Procedure diagram for the cell pellet: pellet 1.5 millilitre aliquots, resuspend each in a different CelLytic B dilution, mix, spin, separate soluble from insoluble fractions.
Procedure strip for the large scale supernatant harvest: pellet the induced culture, keep the supernatant, add protease inhibitor, clarify.
Procedure diagram for large scale pellet lysis: harvest cells, resuspend in CelLytic B with lysozyme and protease inhibitor, shake, add DNase I, spin, collect the soluble fraction.
Procedure diagram for Ni-NTA purification: spin off the storage buffer, equilibrate, add imidazole to the supernatant and load it, wash three times, elute at 175 g.

Procedure diagram for Ni-NTA column regeneration: make 50 millilitres of MES and sodium chloride buffer, pass 30 millilitres through the column, wash with 30 millilitres of water, store in 20 percent ethanol at 4 degrees.
Procedure diagram for SDS-PAGE: pour resolver and stacker, set the comb, heat samples in Laemmli buffer, load the ladder at both ends, run at 200 then 120 volts.
Procedure diagram for Coomassie staining: wash the gel three times in water, stain for an hour, destain until bands show on a clear background.
Procedure diagram for a Western blot: run the gel, build the transfer sandwich onto PVDF, block in milk, incubate with primary and secondary antibodies, detect by chemiluminescence.

Soil experiment overview: soil medium preparation and sowing, then a salinity arm with pre-treatment, co-treatment at 100 millimolar and further applications at 200 and 300 millimolar, and a heat arm at 37 degrees, ending in fresh weight, root length, harvested seed and rosette area.
Procedure diagram for seed sterilization and germination on half MS plates, cold treatment and vertical growth under white light.
Procedure diagram for transplanting a seven-day-old seedling into a soil pot, supporting it from beneath the cotyledons and washing soil over the roots.
Procedure diagram for post-transplant care: tray watering, stepping down humidity under a lid, alternating fertilizer, staking the inflorescence and collecting seed.
Workflow strip for the agar assay: pour plates, sow seeds with the template, vernalize, transfer seedlings to treatment plates, photograph on the black stand.
Seed template for a square agar plate: two rows of nine ticks, the first row 3 centimetres from the top, the rows 5 centimetres apart, and 4 centimetres below the second row.
Timeline of the agar salinity test: sowing and vernalization, germination, transfer onto treatment plates, then daily imaging and harvest into root length, fresh weight and chlorophyll.

Procedure panels for hydroponic salinity testing: overview from seed to germination rack to treatment box, preparing 1 percent MS agar, punching Eppendorf lids, planting seeds in the lids over a 48-well rack, and preparing 3 molar NaCl in half MS medium.

Procedure diagram for heat stress on agar: vernalize and germinate, transfer seedlings to four plates, spray the peptide one day before, on the day, or one day after 37 degree thermopriming, and image daily.
Procedure diagram for chlorophyll extraction: lift and weigh the seedlings, freeze them with steel beads, extract in 80 percent acetone, load a 96-well plate, read at 663 and 645 nanometers.
